mainTopic: Obvious cases in the משנה of the פסח on שבת, what an invalid שחיטה 'fixes' (מקלקל), and רב's rule that an אשם sent to graze needs no עקירה
overview: The עמוד opens by finishing an earlier topic: a פסוק teaches that a כהן eating תרומה anywhere counts like Temple service. The גמרא then asks why our משנה bothers to say that slaughtering the קרבן פסח on שבת for people who cannot eat it makes one חייב. It answers that the obvious cases lead up to the real חידוש, the מחלוקת of רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע. Next, רב הונא בר חיננא asks: if a purely destructive act (מקלקל) on שבת is פטור, why is an invalid שחיטה חייב? Case by case, the גמרא shows that each such שחיטה still 'fixed' something. The parts can stay on the מזבח, a visible טריפה is kept from becoming נבילה, and even slaughter for עבודה זרה removes the animal from אבר מן החי. The גמרא then brings רב's ruling that an אשם sent to graze, if slaughtered without a stated purpose, is valid as an עולה with no עקירה needed. It proves from a משנה that the grazing requirement is only a rabbinic גזירה. Finally רב חסדא begins a challenge to רב הונא from our משנה, and the argument continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: A פסוק shows that eating תרומה counts as Temple service
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the previous discussion with a פסוק showing that eating תרומה outside the מקדש is treated like עבודה in the בית המקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'I have given you your כהונה as a service of gift, and the outsider who comes near shall be put to death.' From this we learn that eating תרומה in the outlying areas was made like the service of the בית המקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the closing line of the previous topic. The גמרא quotes a פסוק to prove that a כהן eating תרומה anywhere is doing something like Temple service.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק calls כהונה an 'עבודת מתנה,' a service that was given as a gift. Since this פסוק appears in the section about the gifts given to כהנים, the gifts themselves, including eating תרומה, count as a kind of עבודה even outside the מקדש. This explains the earlier statement (on the previous עמוד, about רבי טרפון) that eating תרומה is called 'doing עבודה.'

keyTerms.meaning: A service of gift: כהונה given as a present
The portion of produce given to a כהן
Outlying areas, anywhere outside the מקדש
An outsider, a non-כהן

steps.whatToRemember: Eating תרומה, even far from the מקדש, has the status of Temple service.

phrases.english: "A service of gift I give you, your priesthood,
phrases.notes: This פסוק is from במדבר יח:ז.

phrases.english: and the outsider who comes near shall be put to death"
they made the eating of terumah in the outlying areas
like the service of the Temple.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the previous discussion (from the prior עמוד) by giving its scriptural source.
steps.raayaObject: That eating תרומה counts as עבודה even outside the מקדש.
steps.raayaSupportSource: במדבר יח:ז, 'עבודת מתנה אתן את כהונתכם'.

steps.title: Why teach that slaughtering for non-eaters is liable? It is obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of slaughtering the פסח on שבת for people who cannot eat it, and asks why this needs to be said.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'If he slaughtered it for people who cannot eat it, he is חייב.' But that is obvious! Since there, regarding the offering, it is invalid, here, regarding שבת, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes our משנה and complains that its ruling is too obvious to need saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פסח slaughtered שלא לאוכליו is פסול. Slaughtering on שבת is only allowed for a valid offering. Since this offering came out invalid, he simply did a forbidden מלאכה on שבת with no permission, so of course he is חייב a חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: For people who cannot eat it (e.g., not registered or unable to eat)
It is obvious; why say it?
Invalid as an offering
Liable (here: to bring a חטאת for breaking שבת)

steps.confusionAlert: 'התם' (there) refers to the law of the offering itself, and 'הכא' (here) refers to the law of שבת. They are two different questions about the same act.

phrases.english: "He slaughtered it for those who cannot eat it" (is liable).
It is obvious!
Since there (regarding the offering) it is invalid,
here (regarding Shabbat) he is liable!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion on the משנה, unrelated to the תרומה verse.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that שחטו שלא לאוכליו on שבת is חייב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An invalid offering cannot override שבת, so liability is self-evident; the ruling seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The first clause was taught to match the exempt clause
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה listed the liable case only because it was going to list exempt cases afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the end of the משנה (the סיפא) taught cases where he is פטור, the beginning (the רישא) taught cases where he is חייב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of step 2. The obvious חייב case is there to balance the פטור case later in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer admits the ruling teaches nothing new by itself. It was included for style and contrast: the סיפא says that if he slaughtered it for eaters and non-eaters together it is פטור, so the רישא lays out the opposite case first.

keyTerms.meaning: The latter clause of a משנה
The first clause of a משנה
Exempt (no חטאת owed)

phrases.english: Because the latter clause taught "exempt,"
the first clause taught "liable."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Structural/stylistic: the clause exists to parallel another clause.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רישא must be teaching a new חידוש about liability.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רישא was taught only as a contrast to the פטור of the סיפא.

steps.title: But the exempt clause is obvious too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the answer: the סיפא's exemption is also obvious, so it cannot be the reason for the רישא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this too is obvious! Since there, regarding the offering, it is valid, here, regarding שבת, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of step 3. If the סיפא is also obvious, it cannot justify including the רישא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the offering is כשר, slaughtering it on שבת was permitted, so naturally he is פטור. Now both clauses look obvious, and saying 'one obvious clause was taught because of another obvious clause' does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: But this also
Valid as an offering

phrases.english: But this also is obvious,
since there (regarding the offering) it is valid,
here (regarding Shabbat) he is exempt!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the רישא was taught because of the סיפא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סיפא is equally obvious, so it cannot be the 'real' teaching that the רישא is balancing.

steps.title: The non-eaters case was taught alongside the not-for-its-sake case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new answer: the case of שלא לאוכליו was included because the משנה had just taught שחטו שלא לשמו בשבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, since the משנה taught 'he slaughtered it not for its own sake on שבת,' it also taught 'for those who cannot eat it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the first answer ('אלא') and gives a new reason: the case was listed together with a related case, the פסח slaughtered שלא לשמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both cases are about a פסח made invalid by improper intent during slaughter on שבת. Once the משנה listed שלא לשמו, it naturally listed the similar case of שלא לאוכליו with it. The answer shifts the reason from the סיפא to a neighboring case.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; signals dropping the earlier answer
Since it taught (one case, it also taught the next)
Not for its own sake (slaughtered with intent for a different offering)

phrases.english: Rather, since it taught
"He slaughtered it not for its own sake on Shabbat,"
it also taught "for those who cannot eat it."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of step 3 after the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Structural: the case is included because of a parallel neighboring case (איידי).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The case was taught to contrast with the פטור of the סיפא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case was taught alongside שחטו שלא לשמו בשבת.

steps.title: Why is the not-for-its-sake case itself needed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes further: the case of שלא לשמו is also obvious, so why did the משנה need it?
steps.simpleTranslation: And that case itself, why do I need it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now questions the very case it just used as the reason. That case also seems obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פסח slaughtered שלא לשמה is פסול, so slaughtering it on שבת was not permitted, and of course he is חייב. If this case is obvious too, the chain of explanation still needs a real anchor.

keyTerms.meaning: It itself
Why do I need it?

phrases.english: And it itself, why do I need it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the case that step 5 relied on.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's case of שחטו שלא לשמו בשבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That ruling is just as obvious, so it cannot explain why the other obvious case was included.

steps.title: All these cases set up the dispute of רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה listed all these cases because it wanted to present the מחלוקת between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the משנה wanted to present the dispute between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final anchor. The real point of this part of the משנה is the מחלוקת of רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע, and the simpler cases lead up to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Later in the משנה, רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע argue about other offerings slaughtered as a פסח on שבת. That case is truly not obvious. To present it, the משנה first lays out the related simpler cases, so the obvious rulings serve as background.

keyTerms.meaning: To present a dispute

steps.whatToRemember: The obvious cases in the משנה (שלא לאוכליו, שלא לשמו) are there as background, all leading up to the real חידוש: the מחלוקת of רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע.

phrases.english: Because it wanted to present the dispute of
Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 6 and closes the whole 'why is this needed' discussion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Structural: the obvious cases are background for a real dispute.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The case of שלא לשמו has no purpose of its own.
steps.terutzMaskana: It sets the stage for the מחלוקת of רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע.

steps.title: If destructive wounding is exempt, why is invalid slaughter liable?
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר חיננא tells his son to ask רבי זריקא: according to the view that מקלקל בחבורה is פטור, why is slaughtering שלא לאוכליו חייב, since nothing constructive was done?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר חיננא said to his son: When you go before רבי זריקא, ask him: According to the one who says 'one who damages through a wound is exempt,' how can 'he slaughtered it for those who cannot eat it, he is liable' be true? What did he improve?!
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenge opens. רב הונא בר חיננא sends a question through his son: the slaughter ruined the offering, so it should count as a purely destructive act, which some hold is פטור on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שבת, a מלאכה usually must be constructive to make one חייב. Some hold that wounding which only causes damage (מקלקל בחבורה) is פטור. Here the slaughter made the פסח invalid and accomplished nothing useful, so by that view he should be פטור, yet the משנה says חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: One who damages or ruins (a destructive act)
A wound (making blood come out)
What did he improve?
Ask him

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a question about whether the פסח is valid. Everyone agrees it is פסול. The question is about שבת: how can a slaughter that only ruined the animal be a real מלאכה?
steps.whyThisMatters: It ties the laws of the פסח to a basic rule of שבת: that a מלאכה generally needs a constructive purpose to make one חייב.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בַּר חִינָּנָא לִבְרֵיהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Ḥinnana said to his son:
When you go before Rabbi Zerika,
ask him:
According to the one who says "one who damages through a wound is exempt,"
(how can) "he slaughtered it for those who cannot eat it — liable" (be)?
What did he improve?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the same ruling of the משנה (שלא לאוכליו חייב), now challenging it from the laws of שבת instead of asking why it is written.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that שחטו שלא לאוכליו on שבת is חייב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The slaughter invalidated the offering and achieved nothing, making it a purely destructive wound; under the view that מקלקל בחבורה is פטור, he should be exempt.

steps.title: The slaughter fixed something: the parts can stay on the altar
steps.stepSummary: The answer to רב הונא בר חיננא's question: slaughtering שלא לאוכליו is still constructive, because if its parts were brought up on the מזבח they are not taken down.
steps.simpleTranslation: He did fix something: if the parts went up on the altar, they do not come down.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 8. Even a disqualified שחיטה accomplished something positive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was that a ruined act on שבת (מקלקל בחבורה) should be פטור. The answer says this שחיטה is not purely ruining. A קרבן slaughtered שלא לאוכליו has a status where, if its parts were put on the מזבח, they stay and are burned. That small benefit is enough to call the act constructive, so he is חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: He fixed or improved, meaning he did something constructive
If they went up on the altar, they do not come down
The altar

steps.confusionAlert: The קרבן is still פסול. The גמרא is not saying the קרבן is kosher, only that the שחיטה gave it one small useful status.

phrases.english: He fixed something: if they went up [on the altar], they do not come down.
phrases.notes: Refers to the אימורים, the parts burned on the altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question רב הונא בר חיננא sent to רבי זריקא in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a hidden constructive effect of the act
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A disqualified שחיטה accomplishes nothing, so under מקלקל בחבורה פטור he should be exempt.
steps.terutzMaskana: The שחיטה gives the parts the status of אם עלו לא ירדו, which counts as a constructive result.

steps.title: What did he fix with a blemished animal?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the same question about the משנה's case of a בעל מום, where the משנה also says חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: He slaughtered it and it turned out to be blemished, and he is liable. What did he fix?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies the same question to another case in the משנה. If the animal had a blemish, what good did the שחיטה do?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בעל מום is a much weaker קרבן, and normally its parts are taken off the מזבח even if they went up. So the answer from step 9 seems not to work here. The question is how the משנה can call him חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with a physical blemish that disqualifies it as a קרבן
Liable (here, to bring a חטאת)
He slaughtered it

phrases.english: [The משנה says:] If he slaughtered it and it was found to be blemished, he is liable.
What did he fix?

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁחָטוֹ וְנִמְצָא בַּעַל מוּם חַיָּיב, מָה תִּיקֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the 'מה תיקן' question to the next case in the משנה, where step 9's answer seems not to apply.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that one who slaughters a blemished פסח on שבת is חייב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A blemished animal's parts come down from the מזבח, so the שחיטה seems to fix nothing. Under מקלקל בחבורה פטור he should be exempt.

steps.title: A tiny eyelid blemish, following רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is speaking of a minor blemish on the eyelid. According to רבי עקיבא, such parts stay on the מזבח if they went up.
steps.simpleTranslation: He fixed something: the case is a blemish on the eyelid, following רבי עקיבא, who said that if they went up, they do not come down.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by narrowing the case to a very small blemish. With that kind of blemish, the step 9 answer works again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא holds that a tiny blemish like one on the eyelid is not a disgrace to the מזבח. So its parts are not removed once they went up. This means the שחיטה did create a useful status, and he is חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: The eyelid, or the thin membrane of the eye, a spot of a very minor blemish
According to the view of

phrases.english: He fixed something, [when the blemish is] on the eyelid,
and according to רבי עקיבא,
who said: if they went up, they do not come down.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 10 by limiting the case so the step 9 principle still applies.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא) plus following a specific תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any blemish makes the parts come down, so the שחיטה fixed nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is a minor eyelid blemish, where according to רבי עקיבא the parts stay up, so the שחיטה was constructive.

steps.title: What did he fix with a visible טריפה?
steps.stepSummary: From the משנה's exemption for a hidden טריפה, we learn that a visible טריפה makes him חייב. But what did the שחיטה fix there?
steps.simpleTranslation: If he slaughtered it and it was found to be a hidden טריפה, he is exempt. This implies that if it was visible, he is liable. What did he fix?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads an implication from the next part of the משנה. Then it asks the same 'what did he fix' question about a visible טריפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A hidden טריפה is exempt because he could not have known about it. A visible one, which he should have noticed, makes him חייב. But a טריפה can never be a valid קרבן at all. Even the 'if they went up' rule does not help, so what positive result came from the שחיטה?

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with a fatal defect, forbidden even if slaughtered properly
Hidden, such as inside the body
Visible, out in the open
Exempt
This implies (introduces an inference)

phrases.english: [The משנה says:] If he slaughtered it and it was found to be a hidden טריפה, he is exempt.
This implies that if it was visible, he is liable.
phrases.notes: We learn this from the way the משנה is worded.

phrases.english: What did he fix?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next case in the משנה and repeats the 'מה תיקן' challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implied ruling that slaughtering a visible טריפה פסח on שבת makes one חייב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A טריפה is totally unfit, even for the מזבח, so the שחיטה seems to be pure ruining. Under מקלקל בחבורה פטור he should be exempt.

steps.title: The slaughter kept it from becoming נבילה
steps.stepSummary: The constructive effect is that a properly slaughtered טריפה is not נבילה, so it does not carry the severe טומאה of a carcass.
steps.simpleTranslation: He fixed something: he removed it from the status of נבילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that even a טריפה gains something from proper שחיטה. It will not become a נבילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a טריפה dies by itself, it becomes נבילה, which is מטמא those who touch or carry it. A proper שחיטה prevents that טומאה. The benefit here is not about the מזבח but about טהרה, and it is still a real improvement.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that died without proper שחיטה, which is a source of טומאה
To take out of the status of

steps.whatToRemember: Each case has its own 'fix': שלא לאוכליו, where the parts stay on the מזבח; a tiny eyelid blemish, following רבי עקיבא; and a visible טריפה, where it does not become נבילה.

phrases.english: He fixed something: he took it out of the status of נבילה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 12 with a different kind of benefit, one about טומאה rather than the מזבח.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A טריפה gains nothing from שחיטה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Proper שחיטה keeps it from being נבילה and its טומאה, which is a constructive result.

steps.title: רבינא: what was fixed by slaughtering for idolatry?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא brings a ברייתא: one who slaughters a חטאת on שבת outside the מקדש for עבודה זרה brings three חטאות. What did he fix there?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא challenged this: There is a ברייתא that says one who slaughters a חטאת on שבת, outside, for idolatry, is liable to bring three sin-offerings for it. What did he fix?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא attacks the 'something was fixed' approach with a new source. Here none of the earlier answers seem to fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא counts a חטאת for חילול שבת, which assumes the שחיטה was constructive. But an animal slaughtered for עבודה זרה is itself מטמא, so 'it is not נבילה' does not help. Slaughtering outside also means it could never go on the מזבח. So what was fixed? The answer comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Strongly challenged it
Outside the מקדש (שחוטי חוץ)
Idolatry
Three sin-offerings: for שבת, for שחוטי חוץ, and for עבודה זרה

phrases.english: Ravina challenged it:
That which was taught [in a baraita]:
One who slaughters a sin-offering on Shabbat
outside [the Temple] for idolatry
is liable for it to bring three sin-offerings.
What did he fix?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the whole 'מה תיקן' approach with an outside ברייתא where the earlier answers do not apply.
steps.kashyaTarget: The approach that every חייב שחיטה on שבת must have a constructive effect
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Slaughter outside the מקדש for עבודה זרה fixes nothing. It cannot go on the מזבח, and it is מטמא anyway, so the נבילה answer does not help. Yet the ברייתא makes him חייב for שבת.

steps.title: The slaughter removed it from אבר מן החי
steps.stepSummary: רב עוירא answers רבינא's challenge. Even the slaughter of a חטאת on שבת for עבודה זרה accomplished something: it removed the animal from the category of אבר מן החי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עוירא said: The slaughter does fix something, because it takes the animal out of the category of 'a limb from a living animal'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 14: what did the person 'fix' with his slaughter in רבינא's ברייתא?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Meat cut from a living animal is forbidden even to a בן נח. Once the animal is slaughtered, that איסור no longer applies, even if the meat stays forbidden for other reasons. So the slaughter had a real positive effect, and the rule from earlier still holds.

keyTerms.meaning: A limb or meat taken from a living animal, forbidden even to non-Jews
Out of the category of

phrases.english: Rav Avira said:
That he takes it out of the category of a limb from a living animal.
phrases.notes: Even a non-Jew is liable for eating it. After the animal is slaughtered, that איסור is gone.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב עַוִּירָא: שֶׁמּוֹצִיאוֹ מִידֵי אֵבֶר מִן הַחַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge raised in Step 14
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a hidden constructive effect of the slaughter
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The slaughter in רבינא's ברייתא seemed to fix nothing at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: The slaughter took the animal out of the איסור of אבר מן החי, so it did accomplish something.
steps.whatToRemember: In every case the גמרא raised, the slaughter achieved something positive: for שלא לאוכליו, the parts stay on the מזבח; for a minor eyelid blemish, the same, following רבי עקיבא; for a visible טריפה, it does not become נבילה; and here, it is no longer אבר מן החי.

steps.title: An אשם sent to graze and slaughtered without a stated purpose is valid as an עולה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the משנה's next case. רב הונא quotes רב: an אשם that was sent to graze, if slaughtered without stating a purpose, is כשר as an עולה. The גמרא infers that רב does not require עקירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'He slaughtered it and it became known' and so on. רב הונא said in the name of רב: An אשם that was sent off to graze, if someone slaughtered it without saying what it was for, is valid as an עולה. So it seems רב holds that you do not need to 'uproot' its old status.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next phrase of the משנה ('שחטו ונודע'). It then brings רב's related ruling about an animal whose original purpose has fallen away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once an אשם's owner dies or gets כפרה through another animal, this אשם is sent to graze. Its money is meant for an עולה. רב says that if it is slaughtered with no stated purpose, it counts as an עולה. The word 'אלמא' shows the גמרא inferring that no active עקירה, meaning a declaration removing its אשם identity, is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: A guilt-offering
Was sent away to graze (until it gets a blemish)
Without specifying its purpose
A burnt-offering
Uprooting, meaning actively removing the animal's original status
Apparently, which shows that (introduces an inference)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the animal stopped being an אשם in category. It is still an אשם in origin. רב is teaching how it may be used in practice now that its original purpose has fallen away.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling connects to the משנה's case of a קרבן פסח whose owners died. That case also involves an offering whose original purpose has fallen away.

phrases.english: [The משנה said:] He slaughtered it and it became known, etc.
phrases.notes: The full line in the משנה: the פסח was slaughtered, and then it became known that its owners had died.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said in the name of Rav:
A guilt-offering that was sent off to graze,
and someone slaughtered it without specifying its purpose,
it is valid as a burnt-offering.
Apparently he holds:
It does not require uprooting.
phrases.notes: You don't have to say anything out loud to take away its status as an אשם.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב: אָשָׁם שֶׁנִּיתַּק לִרְעִיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next clause of the משנה and opens a new discussion
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אשם sent to graze, if slaughtered without a stated purpose, is כשר as an עולה. No עקירה is needed.

steps.title: Then it should be valid even before it was sent to graze
steps.stepSummary: If no עקירה is needed, an אשם whose owner already got כפרה should be valid as an עולה even before it was formally sent to graze.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then even when it was not yet sent to graze, it should also be valid!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's ruling. It asks why the act of sending the animal to graze should make any difference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the owner gets כפרה through another animal, this animal is already headed toward becoming an עולה. If no uprooting is needed, the formal sending to graze adds nothing. So the animal should be valid as an עולה right away. Yet רב limited his ruling to an animal that 'ניתק'.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Also

phrases.english: If so,
even when it was not sent off [to graze], it should also be valid!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי כִּי לֹא נִיתַּק נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the limit in רב's ruling, based on the inference just made
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's requirement that the אשם was 'ניתק לרעיה'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If no עקירה is needed, the formal sending to graze should make no difference.

steps.title: A rabbinic decree: after כפרה, because of before כפרה
steps.stepSummary: By strict law the animal would be valid as an עולה even before it is sent to graze. The רבנן decreed against this so people would not confuse it with an אשם whose owner has not yet gotten כפרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a decree about the animal after atonement, because of the animal before atonement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The requirement that the animal be sent to graze is only a rabbinic safeguard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the owner gets כפרה, the animal is fully an אשם and would never be valid as an עולה. After כפרה, by strict law it could already be used as an עולה. The רבנן worried people would mix up the two stages, so they required the clear step of sending it to graze before treating it as an עולה.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic decree made as a safeguard
Atonement (here, the owner achieving it through a different animal)
Because of, out of concern for

phrases.english: It is a decree regarding [an אשם] after atonement
because of [an אשם] before atonement.

steps.triggerLanguage: גְּזֵירָה לְאַחַר כַּפָּרָה אַטּוּ לִפְנֵי כַפָּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 17
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rabbinic decree (גזירה) explains the extra requirement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since no עקירה is needed, the rule should apply even without the sending to graze.
steps.terutzMaskana: By strict law it does apply right after כפרה. The requirement to send it to graze is only a rabbinic safeguard.

steps.title: Bringing a source: the משנה about an אשם whose owner died or got כפרה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source for its claim and starts quoting a משנה. That משנה brings three opinions (the תנא קמא, רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע) on what to do with an אשם whose owner died or already got כפרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do you say this? As we learned in a משנה: An אשם whose owner died, or whose owner got atonement, should graze until it gets a blemish. Then it is sold and its money goes to a communal free-will offering. רבי אליעזר says: it should be left to die. רבי יהושע says: it should be sold, and he should bring an עולה with its money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a proof by quoting a משנה. The actual proof from it will come in the next step, so this step is preparing the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא wants to show that after כפרה the animal is, by strict law, already fit as an עולה, and that the grazing rule is only a גזירה. The משנה it quotes gives three views on the fate of such an אשם. The proof will be drawn from the details of these views.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do you say this? (a request for a source)
Until it becomes unfit, meaning it develops a blemish
A free-will offering (here, a communal one)
Its money (the sale price)

phrases.english: And from where do you say this? As we learned [in a משנה]:
A guilt-offering whose owner died
or whose owner achieved atonement [through another animal],
should graze until it becomes unfit [with a blemish],
and it is sold, and its money goes to a [communal] free-will offering.
Rabbi Eliezer says: It should be left to die.
Rabbi Yehoshua says:
It is sold, and he brings a burnt-offering with its money.
phrases.notes: Here the owner brings the עולה for himself, not for the community.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for and begins to supply a source for the claim in Step 18
steps.raayaObject: That an אשם whose owner already got כפרה is, by strict law, already fit as an עולה, and that the grazing requirement is only a גזירה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about an אשם whose owner died or got כפרה, with the views of the תנא קמא, רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע
steps.confusionAlert: The proof is not finished here. This step only quotes the משנה. The point the גמרא draws from it comes next.

steps.title: Its money may become an עולה, but not the animal itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws the inference from רבי יהושע: the money of the leftover אשם may buy an עולה, but the animal itself may not be offered as one. The reason must be a decree: after כפרה is forbidden because of before כפרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: With its money, yes, but the animal itself, no. This is because the רבנן decreed against an אשם after כפרה because of an אשם before כפרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof it started in step 19. It points out exactly what רבי יהושע allows and what he forbids, and explains the reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע lets the money of the leftover אשם buy an עולה. That shows that, by strict law, this animal is already fit to be an עולה. So why may the animal itself not be offered? Only because of a decree, so people will not confuse it with an אשם whose owner has not yet gotten כפרה. This is exactly what the גמרא claimed in step 18.

keyTerms.meaning: With its money (the money from selling the animal)
Its body, meaning the animal itself
He (the רבנן) made a decree
Because of (a protective decree made because of a different case)
Atonement; here, the owner already got atonement through a different animal

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the animal is truly unfit as an עולה. By strict law it is fit, and that is why its money may buy an עולה. The ban on offering the animal itself is only a rabbinic decree.

phrases.english: With its money, yes,
phrases.notes: The money from selling the leftover אשם may buy an עולה.

phrases.english: but the animal itself, no.
phrases.notes: The animal itself may not be offered as an עולה.

phrases.english: because he decreed against after atonement
phrases.notes: An אשם whose owner already got atonement.

phrases.english: because of before atonement.
phrases.notes: An אשם whose owner has not yet gotten atonement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof begun by quoting the משנה in step 19.
steps.raayaObject: The claim from step 18 that an אשם after כפרה is fit as an עולה by strict law, but the רבנן decreed against it.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהושע's ruling in the quoted משנה: the money buys an עולה, but the animal itself is not offered.

steps.title: The proof is accepted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the proof works: there really is a decree against offering an אשם after כפרה, because of an אשם before כפרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this that it is so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the proof and closes this part of the discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With 'שמע מינה', the explanation from step 18 is confirmed. רב can hold that no עקירה is needed and still require the animal to first be sent to graze, because of the rabbinic decree.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it: the proof is accepted

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב, an אשם after כפרה is fit as an עולה by strict law, even without עקירה. Only a decree by the רבנן requires it to first be sent to graze, so it is not confused with an אשם before כפרה.

phrases.english: Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the inference made in step 20.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The decree against offering an אשם after כפרה as an עולה, before it is sent to graze, is confirmed.

steps.title: רב חסדא challenges רב הונא from our משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא raises an objection to רב הונא's view that no עקירה is needed. He begins by quoting our משנה about a פסח slaughtered on שבת when it later became known that the owners had pulled out of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא raised an objection to רב הונא: If he slaughtered it and it then became known that the owners had withdrawn from it, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenge begins. The גמרא is setting up the next move by quoting the source רב חסדא will use. The actual argument continues on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now, the גמרא defended the idea that no עקירה is needed. Now רב חסדא attacks that idea using our own משנה. The משנה rules that someone who slaughtered such a פסח on שבת is exempt, because he slaughtered with permission. רב חסדא will argue that this ruling does not fit with רב הונא's view.

keyTerms.meaning: The owners of the offering
They withdrew their hand: they pulled out of this קרבן and signed up for another

phrases.english: Rav Chisda raised an objection to Rav Huna:
phrases.notes: He's about to challenge him from a משנה or ברייתא.

phrases.english: If he slaughtered it and it became known
that the owners had withdrawn from it, etc.,
phrases.notes: The משנה continues: or they died or became impure. He is exempt because he slaughtered with permission.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the previous discussion closes, a new attack on רב הונא's position from step 16 begins.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's statement in the name of רב that no עקירה is needed (step 16).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Our משנה's ruling about a פסח whose owners withdrew will be shown not to fit the view that no עקירה is needed. The full argument continues on the next עמוד.
